program: dup [ 1 add ] map [ [ lt? ] swap cons ] map swap [ filter ] fold uncons swap drop
notes: Each x becomes the filter (x+1 lt?), i.e. keep y <= x; folding filter over those predicates from xs leaves only copies of the smallest, and the head is taken. Replaces #155's 7-atom ifte combine.

program: [ quote [ eq? ] cat ] map [ [ false eq? ] cat ] map over [ filter ] fold eq? quote [ ] filter 0 [ drop 1 add ] fold
notes: Each y becomes the 4-atom filter (y eq? false eq?); folding filter over them removes from xs every value seen in ys, so the lists are disjoint iff xs survives unchanged. The eq? bool becomes 0/1 by counting it through [ ] filter.

program: over [ drop 1 ] map [ [ add ] swap cons ] map nil [ map 0 cons ] fold swap [ lt? ] swap cons filter swap [ drop uncons drop ] fold
notes: Positions 0..n-1 by the adder idiom over (1 add) closures seeded with nil, the positions below count (min(count, n) of them, so no clamp), then one uncons drop of xs per kept position.

program: nil [ cons ] fold dup [ 1 sub quote ] map [ [ swap lt? ] cat ] map over [ filter ] fold 0 [ swap drop ] fold [ sub ] swap cons map [ [ mul ] swap cons ] map 1 quote [ map 1 cons ] fold [ 0 eq? false eq? ] filter 0 [ drop 1 add ] fold 1 sub
notes: Reversed xs, its maximum m by folding filter over (x-1 swap lt?), the gaps x - m (zero exactly at a maximum), prefix products of the gaps by the adder idiom with (d mul) closures, which stay nonzero until the first maximum; count the nonzero ones and drop the empty product.

program: dup nil [ cons ] fold cat dup uncons drop [ quote ] map [ [ swap sub ] cat ] map [ [ uncons ] swap cat ] map swap [ i quote cat ] fold dup uncons drop [ 1 add ] map [ [ lt? ] swap cons ] map swap [ filter ] fold 0 [ swap drop ] fold 0 swap sub
notes: xs followed by its reverse, so the neighbour differences from a rotate-fold of (uncons x swap sub) closures come in both signs with a 0 at the fold (the one-element default); the minimum of those by (v+1 lt?) filters, read off the last survivor so the leftover head never counts, negated.
